html:
The Skirmish at Bender took place on 1 February 1713 at Bender, an Ottoman fortress on the Dniester in today's Moldova, when Ottoman troops and Tatars stormed the camp of King Charles XII of Sweden.

Charles had fled south after his defeat by Russia at the Battle of Poltava in 1709. The Ottomans sheltered him at Bender for years while he plotted to bring them into war against Peter the Great. When he outstayed his welcome and refused to leave, the sultan ordered his removal. Charles and a few dozen men held a house for hours before he was captured. The fortress, built by the Ottomans in 1538, still stands in the breakaway region of Transnistria.
